claim: How advanced the working machinery is, kept deliberately separate from period so a feudal world can carry magitech and a far-future one can be pre-industrial. It decides whether a character reaches for a torch, a switch or a hologram.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: torch, oil lamp, hand tools, no machinery
steam engine, iron machinery, smokestack, rivets
incandescent bulb, exposed wiring, utility pole, analog switch
computer monitor, crt screen, keyboard, led display
holographic display, floating ui, drones, wireless antenna
cybernetic implants, neon circuitry, augmented visor, wired ports
spaceship hull, airlock, control console, starship interior
magic circle, glowing runes, arcane machinery, enchanted device

review.issue: pre_industrial ends on "no machinery", a negation that tends to summon machinery — the failure is doubly likely here because the surrounding subject (stadium, floodlights) is loudly electric.
review.fix: Positive only: "torch, oil lamp, hand tools, wooden cart". Push "machinery, wires, electric light" into the negative prompt if the floodlights bleed through.
